The second oath to not eat has no effect in terms of eating forbidden foods, so why should one be liable for breaking it? column13: And were His essential force to depart from the most minute creature for a fraction of a second, it would instantly dissolve into absolute nothingness, for all is but an expansion of His Essence. Context and connection to Ohr Zarua LaTzadik: In Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Novellae, Rambam, Kriat Shema 1, Rav Tzadok cites this commentary and philosophical-halakhic exposition (Mishneh Torah, Reading the Shema 1:2) to illuminate his exposition here (“wrote: that the intention of the Pri Chadash was to prove this from the fact that our Master [Maimonides] cited that teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha, that the section of Shema preceded Vehayah [Im Shamoa]...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the hidden light of Torah, the spiritual root of the letters and mitzvot, and the halakhic-aggadic synthesis developed in Ohr Zarua LaTzadik.

column11: Berakhot 4b: ‘In this baraita, the Master said that when one returns from work in the evening, he enters the synagogue, recites Shema, and prays. From this baraita, we see that at night, just as during the day, one first recites Shema and then prays.
